speaker: Doctor
text: I can see you mentioned the history but no details were provided. Please tell me exactly how your right groin pain started and what position your leg is currently in after the rear-end collision. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray Findings: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That leg position—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is highly characteristic of an anterior hip dislocation, which contradicts the appendicitis diagnosis. Did you hear a "pop" at the moment of impact, and can you move your hip or foot at all? REQUEST TEST: MRI Hip. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Hip Findings: Confirms posterior dislocation of the right hip with associated soft tissue injury. The leg position described (shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated) is consistent with posterior dislocation, not anterior dislocation. No acute fracture seen on MRI sequences. Appendicitis is unlikely given the mechanical nature of the injury and imaging findings.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Dislocation of the Right Hip. Given the MRI findings of a posterior dislocation without acute fracture, immediate reduction of the hip is critical to prevent avascular necrosis and cartilage damage. Please proceed to the emergency room for urgent orthopedic consultation and manual reduction.
